headline: Three gates were not doing what their names promised — one switched off for two sessions, one mute for 27 hours, one blind to what it existed to watch. All three fixed, verified in CI, and fully deployed.

items.title: A lossy receipt round trip had silently disabled the S336 content ceiling
items.insight: The board recorded the red uptime-probe cron as an ordering race; reproducing it first showed that fix would not have worked, because the receipt round trip itself was lossy. observationFromReceipt() never restored the three content-clock fields added in S336, the third field forgotten by the reader after retainedForHours in S300 and historyComplete in S316. classify() reads contentLagHours, so every non-probe re-derive collapsed it to null and the alarm S336 built to catch a stranded release could not fire, and had not since the session that created it. Closed as a class with a fixed-point self-test that names no field, plus a companion case proving that guard can actually fail.
items.evidence: build-deploy-currency --self-test 87/87 (was 85) · VERIFIED IN CI: uptime-probe run 33614902860 took the commit-worthy path — the exact failure condition — and exited 0 where it used to print 'receipt drifted'

items.title: Lighthouse CI had been red for 15 runs across 27 hours on a route retired behind an edge redirect
items.insight: /ranks/ was consolidated into /leaderboards/#ranks and answered by a _redirects 301, but three CI audit-target lists still named it. One of them audits the local preview, which serves the built tree with no edge layer, so the redirect that makes production correct cannot apply there and the audit asked for a page that cannot exist. One 404 fails the whole job, so the site's performance gate produced no verdict for over a day and nothing surfaced the silence. Fixed in all four consumers and gated by two structural rules that name no route, both derived from config that already exists.
items.evidence: check-workflow-audit-targets 18/18 self-test · VERIFIED IN CI: Lighthouse run 33612994478 completed SUCCESS on e1c7cef4b, ending 15 consecutive failures across ~27 hours

items.title: Staging parity stopped being an anecdote and became 23 routes and five days
items.insight: check-staging-parity compared a hand-maintained sample of three routes and was structurally incapable of noticing an absent one, which is why S337 could only record /how-we-build/ as prose. It now compares the surface each origin advertises, so coverage is complete and a new route is covered the moment it enters the sitemap. Production advertises 134 routes, staging 115, 23 missing, and staging's build-sha reports 94e78e93 built 2026-08-28. Published with gating false and the reason on the artifact, because gating on a known-open blocker would be a self-inflicted release outage.
items.evidence: check-staging-parity 26/26 (+7) · api/staging-health.json surfaceParity: production 134 routes, staging 115, 23 missing · staging build-sha 94e78e93 from 2026-08-28, probed live

followUps: [S338][DEPLOY/P1] Find what deploys the Hetzner staging origin and why it stopped on 2026-08-28, refresh it, then flip surfaceParity.gating to true so CANON-007 stops running backwards.

[S338][OBS/P2] Audit every other generator that reads its own receipt back for the D-S338.1 class, with fully-populated fixtures — the existing tests may be green for the same wrong reason this one was.
Both CI signals are confirmed green on the real commit; no further verification is outstanding for D-S338.1 or D-S338.2.
blockers: Staging is 23 advertised routes and five days behind production; the release ceremony verifies against it, so CANON-007 currently runs backwards.
Trusted Types enforce remains held on load order: 31 sink-bearing assets load before ambient-core installs the default policy they depend on (D-S337.3).
Four public tables still have no anonymous read path; the fix is a founder privacy decision, not an implementation gap (D-S336.5).
